candidates.term: The Rival at the Hour Gate
candidates.defline: The Rival stands at your Hour Gate, in plain view: in later life people see your nerve and ask you to back them.
candidates.reading: Your later years stay bold and public, with people coming to you for backing long after others have stopped taking risks. Because being in the contest keeps you feeling alive, you say yes to the young and the daring more than you planned. You find real joy in some of that backing, and you lose part of what you give to people who only wanted the money.
candidates.teaser: You will show the future your nerve: heirs and juniors copy your boldness first. Budget for late generosity, because people will ask, and you will want to say yes.

domain_readings.Wealth: Late money keeps your signature moves: the backing of bold things, the open hand, the requests that arrive dressed as opportunity. The estate survives on one discipline, the yearly number your yes can afford. Set it, give inside it freely, and generosity finishes as legacy instead of leakage.
domain_readings.Growth: Your growth late in life comes through the young and daring: their ventures, their nerve, your seasoned eye on their bets. Mentoring bold people keeps your own boldness fed. Choose proteges the way you once chose risks. Carefully, then completely.

candidates.life_chapter: Your late chapter stays in the game: backing ventures, funding nerve, refusing the spectator seat. The last decades run warmer and more generous than most, and the only threat is unbounded yes. Fence the giving, keep the fire, and the ending reads like a patron’s, not a lesson.
candidates.relations: Heirs and proteges are this seat’s people: young, bold, and drawn to your backing. They copy your nerve before your caution, which is the correct order and an expensive one. Teach the bookkeeping alongside the daring. That pairing is the true inheritance.
candidates.turn_catalyst: Run thin, the patron stays retired: nerve intact, checkbook shy. Back one small bold thing this year. The chapter wants you in it.
candidates.turn_friction: Run heavy, the yes outruns the ledger: every knock answered with funding. Publish your annual number and let it answer the door.
candidates.shadow_line: Overloaded, patronage becomes the last contest: giving to outgive, remembered for the amounts.
candidates.health_line: Your late energy loves the arena more than the armchair: activity sustains you, idleness corrodes. Keep a physical practice with stakes, however small.

Wealth.headline: Your later money goes to the bold.
Wealth.recognition: You back people you believe in, a younger relative's venture or a friend's new start, and you give with an open hand. Because daring is what you admire most, a confident request is hard for you to refuse. Your savings shrink in the years you give without counting, and you know which of your gifts were really losses.
Wealth.lived: Since your late forties people have turned to you for support, younger relatives and friends with plans that needed money. You have said yes more often than you meant to, and you have seen some of it pay off and some of it disappear.
Wealth.ahead: From your late forties the people after you, children or younger relatives or someone you train, start bringing you their plans and asking for support. You spend more on other people's ventures in these years than on your own comfort, and you are glad of most of it.

Growth.headline: You keep growing through the daring young.
Growth.recognition: You grow in later life by watching bold people take risks and judging their bets with an experienced eye. Because risk still interests you, mentoring someone daring keeps your own nerve sharp. You lose interest in cautious company, and you come alive around anyone young enough to try something foolish.
Growth.lived: Since your late forties your learning has come through other people's ventures, the plans you advised on and the risks you watched up close. You have grown sharper each time a younger person asked for your judgement, and you have enjoyed being asked.
Growth.ahead: From your late forties you grow by staying involved, advising and backing people who are still at the start. These years keep your mind quick, and you end them with more nerve than most people half your age.

The Rival stands at your Hour Gate, visible in the last chapters: heirs and juniors copy your nerve first, and people will keep asking you to back them late into life. Some of that backing is your genuine growth, the pleasure of funding the young and the bold. Some is leak wearing a warm face. Decide the number early, the amount your yes can afford each year, and give inside it freely. Boldness with a boundary reads as legacy. Without one it reads as lesson.
